title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (TIPS 1-10Y, $750M cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: TSY: api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations + buybacks_security_details for operation_date=2026-09-29 (pulled twice this session, direct curl and WebFetch, byte-identical) - the operation ran exactly as both schedule editions placed it: 1:40-2:00pm ET, settled 09/30/2026, Liquidity Support, TIPS 1Y to 10Y, max $750 million, 28 eligible issues (91282CFR7 through 91282CPU9), $3,981M offered, $605M accepted (7 issues). Confirmed 2026-09-30 on the operation's own published announcement/results record, superseding the prior EST: tentative-schedule label. Prior estimate provenance retained for the record: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding), reissued 2026-09-09 (masthead 'For Publication September 9, 2026', 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd) with this row verbatim unchanged from the original 'For Publication August 5, 2026' edition (125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35).
notes: CANONICAL FILE written 2026-09-08 during this event's own initial research, from the one proposal that existed for the id (from-treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15, filed the same day); that proposal's read is upheld and sharpened. THE FINDING THAT MAKES IT WORTH TRACKING, off api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations (all 220 operations, both pages, fetched 2026-09-08): this is the ONLY TIPS bucket in the program whose cap actually binds — 7 of 8 operations filled 98-100% of the $750M cap, a 93.7% mean fill that ranks 4th of the program's 15 bucket/type categories, against 22.5% (0 of 4) for its TIPS 10Y-30Y sibling and 10.3% (0 of 9) for the 7Y-10Y nominal bucket. The streak broke on 2026-07-22: $405M accepted, a 54.0% fill, on $3,194M offered (12.7% take share). That is the program's ONLY uncensored measurement of this bucket's price-acceptable supply — the other seven are censored at the cap — and it reads BELOW the cap. The mechanism is measurable rather than inferred: total par offered has fallen $6,512M -> $3,194M (-51%) across the eight operations while the maturity window's front rolled a full year (2026-10-15 -> 2027-10-15) and the count of eligible sub-1%-coupon lines fell 14 -> 10. Structurally this is also the only buyback bucket that mixes all four TIPS tenors ever issued: its 27-line July list spans original 30-Year TIPS auctioned 1998-04-08 and 1999-04-07, 20-Year TIPS from 2008/2009, negative-real-yield 10-Year TIPS from 2020-2022, and 5-Year TIPS from 2024/2025 — 27 years of issuance vintage, the exact inverse of the 10Y-30Y bucket, which contains only 30-year paper. Two schedule firsts: 09-29 settles 09/30/2026, the last business day of September AND of Q3 (no prior operation in this bucket settled on a month-end business day), and the August-refunding schedule gives this bucket two rows ($750M each, 9/29 and 10/21) against one $500M TIPS 10Y-30Y row. sb0607 (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200) names 'nominal coupon securities' only, so this $750M cap is untouched inside the 09-09 -> 11-04 doubled window. Low impact is honest about size: ~$45B of TIPS issuance is scheduled in the same corridor (09-17 10Y reopening, 10-22 new 5Y), a 60:1 issuance-to-cap ratio. Estimate-labelled; nothing here licenses an entry. PULSE 2026-09-15 (D-14), three updates. (1) The reissued schedule leaves this row verbatim unchanged at $750M while nominal long caps triple - the largest open schedule risk is retired. (2) The sibling TIPS 10Y-30Y label filled its $500M cap for the FIRST time on 2026-09-15 (0/4 -> 1/5, mean fill 22.5% -> 38.0%) on $2,088M offered, 2.03x its own four-operation mean and 1.50x its prior maximum, with its eligible count flat at 16 - a tape-driven offer impulse, not an inventory one, which raises this operation's fill odds while putting the draining-inventory mechanism at real risk. (3) The framing above needs one correction the program itself supplied: on 2026-09-10 the nominal 10Y-20Y bucket ran at a tripled $6B cap and took $5,187M (86.5%), its first non-fill in 26 operations, take share 27.0% -> 49.5% - so every 100% fill in the ranking is cap-censored, and 'the only bucket whose cap binds' is a statement about cap size relative to the offer pool rather than about a bucket-specific price filter. The relative ranking survives: TIPS 1Y-10Y 93.7%, 5th of the 12 categories with n >= 4, against 38.0% for TIPS 10Y-30Y and 10.3% for 7Y-10Y nominals. Leg 11's scale deflator is now stronger, not weaker: the 9/17 10Y TIPS reopening is ANNOUNCED at $19.0B (auctions_query, announcement date 2026-09-10), 25:1 against this $750M cap on that leg alone. PULSE 2026-09-22 (D-7): schedule still unreissued (byte-identical to 09-15, md5 c49a5351...). Both weekly falsifiers resolved toward the base case - FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4% on 9/16 as priced, and the 9/17 10Y TIPS reopening (91282CRE3) priced 21.5bp cheaper in real-yield terms than the 07-23 original auction (2.653% vs 2.438%) on a softer 2.24x bid-to-cover. No new TIPS 1Y-10Y bucket operation exists yet (buybacks_operations re-pulled, 223 rows, still stops at 07-22 for this bucket) and the 09-29 terms remain unpublished ahead of 9/28. Treasury's own real curve put 5Y real at a fresh 2026 high (2.55 on 09-18) and 5s30s real at a fresh 2026 low (0.52 on 09-21), extending leg 8's bear-flattening; the 5Y breakeven (~2.33) stayed inside its 2.16-2.72 range despite the hike and a further Brent spike (FRED stale at $130.80 as of 09-15, sourced to a live US-Iran war tape per the unsc-middle-east-2334 sibling ledger, not independently re-verified past 09-15 here). Full workup: docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-tips-1y10y-2026-09-29.md CLOSE-OUT 2026-09-30 (D+1): the operation ran as scheduled and all four registered forward tests scored pass. api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations + buybacks_security_details (operation_date=2026-09-29, pulled twice this session, direct curl and WebFetch, byte-identical): 28 eligible / 7 accepted, $3,981M offered, $605M accepted (80.7% of the $750M cap, 15.2% take share) - inside the 09-08 stance's own $500M-750M base case on offers under $5.0B. The eligible list matched leg 10's derivation exactly (91282CFR7 through 91282CPU9, 91282CRE3 excluded, 91282CPU9 present for the first time and taking $0, confirming the derivation's own caveat about near-par recently-issued paper). 912828ZZ6 (leg 7's 2020-vintage negative-real-yield line) priced $150M at 91.181, a further -1.821pt mark-down from its 93.002 print on 07-22. Treasury's own real curve: 5Y real 2.72% on 09-29, a fresh 2026 high; BE5 ~2.34%, still inside the 2.16-2.72% range. status flipped estimate -> confirmed, source EST: -> TSY:, on the operation's own announcement/results primaries.
